correctness.rationale: Conserved H=x-log x+y^2/2 and xdot=-xy, ydot=x-1 imply a unique initial small-x exit on negative-y branch for sufficiently small epsilon. At exit y=-z, x=s/z, energy equation z^2/2+log z+s/z=L+eta^2/2+log s+epsilon. Exact physical time integral of 1/(1-X(y)) has boundary layer s/z^2+O(z^-3), which cancels -s/R^2 from endpoint expansion, leaving time eta+sqrt(2L)+(eta^2+2log s-log(2L))/(2sqrt(2L))+O((log L)^2/L^(3/2)). Independent mpmath high-precision Lambert W quadrature at eta=0,s=1,L=100 yields 13.95456467198 against 13.95481181679 asymptotic and reconstructs Gaussian inverse. Fixed positive s, bounded eta only.
